title: Sharp maps glue over special cofibrant colimit diagrams
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, weak equivalences and monomorphisms of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], and sharp maps and homotopy-cartesian squares as explicitly defined in [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus]. Let $I$ be a small category and $p:U\to V$ a natural transformation of $I$-diagrams of simplicial sets. Assume each $p_i:U_i\to V_i$ is sharp and each naturality square for an arrow of $I$ is homotopy cartesian. Suppose one of the following holds:
(1) $I=\mathbf N$ with its usual order, and every successive map in each of $U,V$ is a monomorphism.
(2) $I$ is the span $1\leftarrow0\to2$, and the maps $U_0\to U_2$ and $V_0\to V_2$ are monomorphisms.
(3) $I=\mathcal P_{<}(S)$ is the inclusion poset of all proper subsets of a finite set $S$, including the empty subset when it is proper; both diagrams are cofibrant in the explicit sense that, for each proper $T\subset S$, the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_{R\subsetneq T}U_R\to U_T$ is a monomorphism, and likewise for $V$.
Then $\operatorname{colim}_I U\to\operatorname{colim}_I V$ is sharp, and for every $i\in I$ the canonical square $U_i\to\operatorname{colim}_I U$ over $V_i\to\operatorname{colim}_I V$ is homotopy cartesian. No Kan or Reedy fibrancy is assumed. The empty indexing category in (3), when $S=\varnothing$, is included.
Moreover, let $e:E\to H$ be any sharp map, and let $U_i\to E$ and $V_i\to H$ be compatible cocones commuting with $p$ and $e$. If every component cocone square $U_i\to E$ over $V_i\to H$ is homotopy cartesian, then the induced square $\operatorname{colim}_I U\to E$ over $\operatorname{colim}_I V\to H$ is homotopy cartesian.

source.place: Proposition 8.1 (1)-(3), printed p. 15, and the relative-cocone consequence: Proposition 6.4 and Corollary 6.6 for finite subset colimits, the proper-model pushout gluing argument and sequential weak-equivalence invariance. Specialization to simplicial sets. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy theorem.

proof.text: All colimits below are the degreewise set colimits. In sets over a fixed set $B$, an element of a colimit is a representative $(i,x)$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by transition maps, all of which preserve its image in $B$. Restricting these representatives and relations to a fixed fiber proves $T\times_B\operatorname{colim}_i Z_i\cong\operatorname{colim}_i(T\times_B Z_i)$ for every diagram over $B$; this is [lem-coef-sset-pullback-preserves-colimits]. Apply this in each simplicial degree: it is natural in all operators, so is an isomorphism of simplicial sets. Pullbacks preserve monomorphisms degreewise. The simplex criterion also gives the following local test: if $\coprod_a B_a\to B$ is degreewise surjective and each $B_a\times_B E\to B_a$ is sharp, then $E\to B$ is sharp. Indeed every $n$-simplex $\Delta^n\to B$ lifts to one $B_a$ by choosing a preimage of its representing $n$-simplex. For every $\delta:\Delta^m\to\Delta^n$, the comparison in criterion (iii) is therefore the comparison for that sharp pullback. This proves the test without requiring the cover to be a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 3.7, Remark 4.2 and Proposition 5.1(P4); explicit degreewise arguments.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cofibrant-subset-colimit-decomposition] to each of the diagrams $U,V$ whenever $|S|\geq1$. Thus, after choosing $s\in S$ and putting $S'=S\setminus\{s\}$, the diagrams $A_R=Z_R$, $B_R=Z_{R\cup\{s\}}$ on proper subsets of $S'$ are cofibrant, and the original colimit is the pushout $C_Z\amalg_{\operatorname{colim}A}\operatorname{colim}B$, with $C_Z=Z_{S'}$. In particular the leg $\operatorname{colim}A\to C_Z$ is mono in each of the two spans. The construction is natural in $Z$, so a transformation of the original diagrams induces a transformation of precisely these pushout spans. These are the combinatorial inputs for the two finite inductions below; none asserts sharpness or homotopy-cartesianness.

An objectwise weak equivalence between two cofibrant diagrams indexed by proper subsets of $S$ induces a weak equivalence on colimits. Prove this auxiliary assertion by induction on $|S|$. For $|S|=0$, both colimits are empty and the induced map is the identity; for $|S|=1$ the colimit is the component at the empty subset. For $|S|\geq2$, use the preceding decomposition for both diagrams. Restrictions $A,B$ are cofibrant diagrams on proper subsets of the smaller set $S'$, so both induced maps on their colimits are weak equivalences by induction. The component map at $S'$ is also a weak equivalence. The maps $\operatorname{colim}A\to C_Z$ in both spans are mono, so the pushout clause of the cited weak-equivalence gluing theorem proves the inductive step. In cases (1) and (2) the analogous objectwise weak-equivalence invariance is already precisely its filtered-poset and pushout clauses. Thus all three shapes have the invariance needed below.

source.place: Corollary 6.6, proved with Proposition 6.4 and the pushout cube lemma.

proof.text: Prove the relative-cocone conclusion now, independently of the sharpness conclusion, to make it available as an induction hypothesis later. Put $P_i=V_i\times_H E$. Since $e:E\to H$ is sharp, each assumed cocone square gives a weak equivalence $U_i\to P_i$ by the strict-pullback comparison criterion; these maps form a natural transformation by the cocone equations. The diagram $P$ meets the same monomorphism hypotheses as $V$. In case (3), all predecessor objects map to $V_T$, so the first step identifies its latching map with $(\operatorname{colim}_{R\subsetneq T}V_R)\times_H E\to V_T\times_H E$, a pullback of the latching monomorphism for $V$. Thus $P$ is cofibrant. The weak-equivalence invariance just proved gives $\operatorname{colim}U\to\operatorname{colim}P$ a weak equivalence. The first step identifies $\operatorname{colim}P$ with $(\operatorname{colim}V)\times_H E$. The comparison criterion for the sharp map $e$ proves the asserted homotopy-cartesian square. This includes $I=\varnothing$, where both comparison objects are empty.

source.place: Relative-cocone consequence of Proposition 3.7, Proposition 2.7 and Corollary 6.6; expanded argument.

proof.text: For case (1), write $U_\infty=\operatorname{colim}U_n$, $V_\infty=\operatorname{colim}V_n$, and for a fixed $n$ put $W_m=V_n\times_{V_m}U_m$ for $m\geq n$. Each $W_m\to V_n$ is sharp by base change. The transition $W_m\to W_{m+1}$ is a weak equivalence by the universally base-changed comparison assertion in the sharp-pullback calculus, applied to the naturality square for $m\to m+1$ and $V_n\to V_m$. It is mono: its composite with $W_{m+1}\to U_{m+1}$ is $W_m\to U_m\to U_{m+1}$, a composite of monos, since $V_n\to V_m$ is mono. Hence every $W_n\to W_m$ is a weak equivalence. Apply filtered weak-equivalence invariance to the natural map from the constant diagram $W_n$ to this tail, giving $U_n=W_n\to\operatorname{colim}_{m\geq n}W_m$ a weak equivalence. The tail is cofinal by the elementary replacement $m\mapsto\max(m,n)$. In each degree a sequence of injective maps has injective structure maps into its union, so $V_m\to V_\infty$ is mono and $V_n\times_{V_\infty}U_m=V_n\times_{V_m}U_m$ for $m\geq n$. The first step therefore identifies the tail colimit with $V_n\times_{V_\infty}U_\infty$. The map from this colimit to $V_n$ is sharp: for a weak equivalence $T\to T'$ over $V_n$, sharpness of each $W_m$ gives $W_m\times_{V_n}T\to W_m\times_{V_n}T'$ a weak equivalence, and filtered invariance plus the first-step identification proves the same after colimit. The defining equivalence for sharpness then applies. Since $\coprod_n V_n\to V_\infty$ is degreewise surjective, the local test of step 1 proves $U_\infty\to V_\infty$ sharp. The weak equivalences already obtained prove every component square homotopy cartesian by the comparison criterion.

source.place: Proposition 8.1(1) and Lemma 8.2, printed pp. 15-16; expanded tail and sharpness arguments.

proof.text: Here is the weak-equivalence attachment argument needed for the pushout case. Suppose $X\xrightarrow{i}Y$, $X\xrightarrow{f}X'$ has pushout $Y'$ with $g:Y\to Y'$, and maps to $A\to B$ give a commuting diagram $X\to Y$ over $X'\to Y'$ over $A\to B$. Suppose $p:X'\to A$, $pf:X\to A$, and $qg:Y\to B$ are sharp, $f$ is a weak equivalence, and either $i$ or $f$ is mono. Then $q:Y'\to B$ is sharp. Indeed $f$ is a homotopy-cartesian comparison over $\mathrm{id}_A$ between sharp maps, so every pullback of $f$ to $A$ is a weak equivalence. For each $T\to B$, pullback preserves the pushout by step 1, and $T\times_B f=(T\times_B A)\times_A f$ is a weak equivalence. If $i$ is mono, the pushout gluing clause applied to the map of spans $(Y\leftarrow X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X)\to(Y\leftarrow X\xrightarrow{f}X')$ shows $T\times_B g$ is a weak equivalence. If instead $f$ is mono, its pullback is a trivial cofibration; its pushout is a trivial cofibration by the lifting-property definition in the model structure, hence again a weak equivalence. Finally for a weak equivalence $T\to T'$ over $B$, the comparison between pullbacks of $qg$ is a weak equivalence, and the two comparisons induced by $g$ are weak equivalences as just proved. Two-out-of-three proves the comparison for $q$, hence sharpness. The sharpness assertion is recorded separately in [lem-coef-sharp-pushout-attachment-comparison]; the argument above explains its use in the next two reductions.

source.place: Lemma 8.3, printed p. 16; proof using universal comparisons and weak-equivalence gluing.

proof.text: Start case (2) with the additional assumption that both naturality squares are strict pullbacks. In degree $q$, decompose $(V_2)_q$ as the disjoint union of the image of $(V_0)_q$ and its complement. The right pullback identifies $(U_2)_q$ with $(U_0)_q$ and its inverse-image complement. Thus the pushouts are $(V_1)_q$ plus the complement in $(V_2)_q$, and $(U_1)_q$ plus the corresponding complement in $(U_2)_q$. The left pullback gives $(U_0)_q=(U_1)_q\times_{(V_1)_q}(V_0)_q$, even when $V_0\to V_1$ is not injective. Thus pulling the total map back to $(V_1)_q$ returns $(U_1)_q$; pulling it back to $(V_2)_q=(V_0)_q\amalg D_q$ returns $((U_1)_q\times_{(V_1)_q}(V_0)_q)\amalg (U_2′)_q=(U_2)_q$, where $U_2′$ denotes only the degreewise complement. Pulling further back to $(V_0)_q$ returns $(U_0)_q$. These descriptions show that the squares from each of $i=0,1,2$ to the pushouts are strict pullbacks. They hold naturally as squares of simplicial sets since the comparison maps are degreewise bijective; no natural choice of complement is required. The cover $V_1\amalg V_2\to V_1\amalg_{V_0}V_2$ is degreewise surjective and its two pullbacks are $p_1,p_2$, so step 1 gives sharpness of the induced map. Every component square is homotopy cartesian by the definition of sharpness.

source.place: Proposition 8.1(2), case (a), printed p. 17; degreewise complement argument.

proof.text: Next assume only the right square is a strict pullback. Set $U'_0=V_0\times_{V_1}U_1$ and $U'_2=U'_0\amalg_{U_0}U_2$. The comparison $f:U_0\to U'_0$ is a weak equivalence; $U'_0\to V_0$ is sharp by base change. Apply step 6 with $X=U_0$, $Y=U_2$, $X'=U'_0$, $A=V_0$, $B=V_2$: the map $i:U_0\to U_2$ is mono, and the three maps required sharp are respectively $U'_0\to V_0$, $p_0$, and $p_2$. It gives $U'_2\to V_2$ sharp. Moreover $U_2\to U'_2$ is a weak equivalence by the pushout gluing argument with the mono $U_0\to U_2$. The new right square is a strict pullback: degreewise, in a pushout $X'=X\amalg_A A'$ with $A\hookrightarrow X$, if $A$ is exactly the inverse image of $B\hookrightarrow Y$ under $X\to Y$, then $X'$ consists of $A'$ and the unchanged complement of $A$ in $X$, whose image avoids $B$. Consequently $A'$ is exactly the inverse image of $B$ in $X'$. Apply this with $(A,X,A',X',B,Y)=(U_0,U_2,U'_0,U'_2,V_0,V_2)$. The new left square is a pullback by construction, and $U'_0\to U'_2$ is mono as a pushout of the original mono. Step 7 applies. The total pushout is unchanged, since $U_1\amalg_{U'_0}(U'_0\amalg_{U_0}U_2)=U_1\amalg_{U_0}U_2$. Component weak equivalences $U_0\to U'_0$, $U_2\to U'_2$ and two-out-of-three for the strict-pullback comparisons prove the original component squares homotopy cartesian.

source.place: Proposition 8.1(2), case (b), with Lemma 8.4, printed pp. 17-18.

proof.text: For general case (2), put $\widetilde U_0=V_0\times_{V_2}U_2$ and $\widetilde U_1=U_1\amalg_{U_0}\widetilde U_0$. The comparison $f:U_0\to\widetilde U_0$ is a weak equivalence by the given right homotopy-cartesian square. It is mono because its composite with $\widetilde U_0\to U_2$ is the mono $U_0\to U_2$. The map $\widetilde U_0\to V_0$ is sharp. Apply step 6 with $(X,Y,X',A,B)=(U_0,U_1,\widetilde U_0,V_0,V_1)$, using the alternative that $f$ is mono, to obtain $\widetilde U_1\to V_1$ sharp and $U_1\to\widetilde U_1$ a weak equivalence (the pushout of a trivial cofibration). The new left square is homotopy cartesian: its comparison $\widetilde U_0\to V_0\times_{V_1}\widetilde U_1$ is a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three, since the comparison from $U_0$ to $V_0\times_{V_1}U_1$ is one and the latter pullback comparison induced by $U_1\to\widetilde U_1$ is one. For this last assertion, regard $U_1\to\widetilde U_1$ as a square over $\mathrm{id}_{V_1}$ between sharp maps, and use the universally base-changed comparison in the sharp calculus. The new right square is a strict pullback and $\widetilde U_0\to U_2$ is mono since $V_0\to V_2$ is. Step 8 therefore applies. The total pushout is again unchanged by associativity, and the component weak equivalences, together with the comparison criterion and two-out-of-three, give the original component squares. This completes case (2).

source.place: Proposition 8.1(2), case (c), printed p. 18; expanded verification of the modified left square.

proof.text: Prove case (3) by induction on $|S|$. For $S=\varnothing$ the total map is $\varnothing\to\varnothing$, which is sharp because every map to the empty simplicial set has empty domain; there are no component squares. For $|S|=1$ the diagram has its single object $\varnothing$, so the assertion is the assumed sharpness and the identity square. For larger $S$, form $A^U,B^U,C_U$ and $A^V,B^V,C_V$ as in step 2. The induction hypothesis gives sharp maps $a:\operatorname{colim}A^U\to\operatorname{colim}A^V$ and $b:\operatorname{colim}B^U\to\operatorname{colim}B^V$, with all component-to-colimit squares homotopy cartesian.

source.place: Proposition 8.1(3), printed pp. 18-19; induction strengthened with the previously proved relative-cocone consequence.

proof.text: Apply the relative-cocone conclusion of step 4, which was proved for every finite set and uses only cofibrancy of both diagrams, a sharp target and homotopy-cartesian cocone squares, to the shape $\mathcal P_{<}(S')$: take $A^U\to A^V$, cofibrant by [lem-coef-cofibrant-subset-colimit-decomposition], with the cocones to $C_U,C_V$ and sharp target $p_{S'}$. Each cocone square is a naturality square of $p$, hence homotopy cartesian. This gives the homotopy-cartesian square from $a$ to $p_{S'}$. For every $R\subsetneq S'$, paste the naturality square at $R\to R\cup\{s\}$ with the induction square from $B_R$ to $\operatorname{colim}B$ using the sharp pasting assertion of [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus]; the three vertical maps $p_R$, $p_{R\cup\{s\}}$ and $b$ are sharp. This gives homotopy-cartesian cocone squares from $A_R$ to $b$, compatible because the composites $U_R\to U_{R\cup\{s\}}\to\operatorname{colim}B^U$ form the cocone inducing $\operatorname{colim}A^U\to\operatorname{colim}B^U$. Apply step 4 again to these cocones, whose target $b$ is sharp, giving the homotopy-cartesian square from $a$ to $b$.

source.place: Proposition 8.1(3), printed pp. 18-19; induction strengthened with the previously proved relative-cocone consequence.

proof.text: The three maps $a,b,p_{S^{\prime}}$ form the transformation of pushout spans from step 2. Step 11 supplies its two homotopy-cartesian naturality squares. By [lem-coef-cofibrant-subset-colimit-decomposition], the legs $\operatorname{colim}A\to C_Z$ are monomorphisms in both spans. Relabel these as the $0\to2$ legs of case (2), with the $\operatorname{colim}A\to\operatorname{colim}B$ legs as $0\to1$. Apply the span result proved in steps 7–9. It gives sharpness of the total map and homotopy-cartesian squares from $C_Z$, $\operatorname{colim}A$ and $\operatorname{colim}B$ to the total colimits.

source.place: Proposition 8.1(3), printed pp. 18-19; induction strengthened with the previously proved relative-cocone consequence.

proof.text: For a proper subset $T\subset S$ there are three cases. If $T=S'$, use the square from $C_Z$ supplied by the span result of steps 7–9. If $T\subsetneq S'$, paste the induction square from $A_T$ to $\operatorname{colim}A$ with its square to the total colimit. If $s\in T$, write $T=R\cup\{s\}$ with $R\subsetneq S'$ and paste the induction square from $B_R$ to $\operatorname{colim}B$ with its square to the total colimit. All three vertical maps in each pasting are sharp by the original hypotheses, the induction hypothesis, and the span result of steps 7–9. This proves the induction and completes all conclusions, including the relative conclusion already proved in step 4. The induction uses no object indexed by the excluded full subset $S$.

source.place: Proposition 8.1(3), printed pp. 18-19; induction strengthened with the previously proved relative-cocone consequence.
